goal: Record the rejection of job_outbox-boundary enforcement for Import consent as ADR 0016, and make guardImportConsent's refusals durably queryable by completing the refused outbox row with completion_reason = 'import_consent_blocked'.
non_goals: No job_outbox trigger, CHECK constraint, or migration — the Import consent enforcement locus stays ZernioBackfillWorker per spec §5.3, re-affirmed by ADR 0016.
No change to guardImportConsent's proceed/skip decision, its sql.begin serialization, its businesses FOR UPDATE lock, or the importConsentStateSql derived-expiry predicate.

No per-state reason values — one 'import_consent_blocked' member; the specific refusal state (pending | declined | expired | missing) stays in the existing structured log line and is recoverable from businesses.import_decision + import_offer_expires_at.
No HealthAlertPoller check, no Sentry capture, no PostHog event — a refusal is the guard working, not an incident.
No /admin/jobs rendering of completion_reason; SURFACE stays backend.
No completion_reason on guardZernioJobEligibility's three skips (missing row, archived location, subscription guard) — they stay generic completions.
No change to owner_unreachable semantics, its two poller readers, or the tenant-scope allowlist entries that spell its SQL.
No backfill of historical rows; legacy and other-topic rows keep completion_reason NULL.
user_visible_behavior: None for owners — no UI, no notification, no API shape change.

Operator-visible only: a zernio_initial_backfill outbox row refused by guardImportConsent now carries job_outbox.completion_reason = 'import_consent_blocked' instead of NULL, so a policy refusal is separable by SQL from a genuine completed import.
invariants: Invariant #2 (transactional outbox): the reason write happens inside guardImportConsent's existing sql.begin on the same tx handle as the businesses FOR UPDATE — never a second statement outside that transaction.
Spec §5.3 single-owner: importConsentStateSql stays the ONE spelling of the derived-expiry predicate — nothing re-spells it in SQL, PL/pgSQL, or a migration.
Import consent stays fail-closed: only 'accepted' proceeds; every other state and a missing businesses row are skip-as-success (outbox row completed, never failed, thrown, or retried).
#679's data-loss window stays closed: the businesses row lock and the in-transaction outbox completion remain both load-bearing.
owner_unreachable behaviour is unchanged after the helper generalization — same emitted UPDATE, same attempt-guarded CAS, same 0-row warn, same two poller readers.
completion_reason values are written and read only via OUTBOX_COMPLETION_REASON — no bare string literal at any site (CLAUDE.md working rules).
edge_cases: Superseded dispatch attempt: the reason write uses the same attempt-guarded dispatchedRow CAS, so a stale attempt updates 0 rows and warns rather than stamping a reason onto a newer attempt's row.
Missing businesses row (reason 'missing'): still marked import_consent_blocked — a hand-inserted row for a deleted location is a refusal, not a separate class.

Guard-first-then-owner-accepts interleaving (#679): the refused row completes WITH the marker and recordImportDecisionAndEnqueue inserts a fresh runnable row; the marker sits on the old row id and must not make the fresh row look pre-refused.
A row refused as 'pending' whose business later becomes 'accepted': completion_reason stays 'import_consent_blocked' on the historical row — it records what happened, not current state.
checkOwnerUnreachable's `completion_reason IS DISTINCT FROM 'owner_unreachable'` predicate must not be perturbed by a new non-NULL value appearing on a different topic.
Legacy rows enqueued before this change, and every other one of the 32 topics, keep completion_reason NULL.
existing_patterns_to_follow: src/lib/shared/outbox.ts — markOutboxOwnerUnreachable is the exact shape being generalized (dispatchedRow attempt-guarded CAS + warnOutboxNoop on 0 rows); this is its second use, so generalizing is warranted rather than duplicating.
src/lib/shared/outbox-completion-reason.ts — the single-owner vocabulary constant that gains one member.
docs/adr/0010-owner-unreachable-outcome.md — the ADR shape for 'why this outbox outcome is a distinct, durable one'.
docs/adr/0015-consented-import-unflagged-replacement.md — the ADR shape for a locked Review-import decision.
worker/jobs/zernio/job-eligibility.ts guardImportConsent — the one call site; its sql.begin / FOR UPDATE structure is untouched.
src/lib/shared/__tests__/outbox.test.ts 'markOutboxOwnerUnreachable (invariants)' describe block — the unit-test shape for the generalized helper.
worker/jobs/zernio/__tests__/job-eligibility.test.ts — existing 'guardImportConsent …' title convention, matched verbatim by the new titles.

estimated_prod_lines: ±180 (≈50 code across 4 files + ≈130 docs: ADR 0016 ~100, spec §5.3 amendment ~12, CONTEXT.md ~6, CLAUDE.md ~2 — docs/adr and CONTEXT.md count toward this bucket, only docs/superpowers/plans and docs/reviews are excluded)
rollback_plan: Revert the commit. No migration to reverse — job_outbox.completion_reason has existed since migration 083 and is nullable with no CHECK constraint, so historical rows carrying 'import_consent_blocked' are inert after a revert and no reader interprets them. No feature flag, no env var, no data backfill. The helper generalization reverts with the same commit, restoring markOutboxOwnerUnreachable at its single NotificationWorker call site.
observability: Durable signal (new): SELECT completion_reason, count(*) FROM job_outbox WHERE topic = 'zernio_initial_backfill' AND status = 'completed' GROUP BY 1 — an 'import_consent_blocked' bucket counts refusals, the NULL bucket counts genuine imports. Before this change the two were indistinguishable.

Existing signal (unchanged): the structured worker log line 'import consent blocked — skipping backfill' carrying { reason, business_id } — the per-state detail the single marker deliberately does not duplicate.
How I would know it broke — marker regression: a refusal that leaves completion_reason NULL (the pre-change behaviour) means the guard stopped stamping.

How I would know it broke — generalization regression: HealthAlertPoller.checkOwnerUnreachable and NotificationFailoverPoller going quiet, or send_notification rows completing with completion_reason NULL where the owner had zero verified enrollments, means owner_unreachable marking was lost in the refactor.
